title: Sum of inspired oral teaching — as to faith and salvation — is in Scripture
source_text: XXXIII. Verum illud arcte tenemus, summam eorum, quae homines sancti, divino Spiritu acti, docuerunt & prolocuti sunt, quantum ad salutem & fidem sufficit, Scriptura sacra contineri; nec quicquam eos docuisse, quod sit ad religionem alicujus momenti, quod in sacris literis abunde traditum non sit.
pass_a_gloss: But that we tightly hold, that the sum of those things which holy men, moved by the divine Spirit, taught and spoke, as much as suffices for salvation and faith, is contained in sacred Scripture; nor that they taught anything which is of any moment for religion that has not been abundantly handed down in the sacred letters.
pass_b_english: Yet we hold this tightly: the sum of what holy men, moved by the divine Spirit, taught and spoke — so far as suffices for salvation and faith — is contained in sacred Scripture.
They taught nothing of any weight for religion that has not been handed down abundantly in the sacred letters.

lemmas.gloss: moved / driven by the divine Spirit

choices.why: Not every spoken word, but the substance needed for faith.
Contrast with the free concession of XXXII.
